question.text: Which of the following best describes the ongoing servicing role of a mutual fund distributor after a sale?

answer.text: Guaranteeing a minimum return to the investor after the sale is completed
Processing only the initial purchase transaction and collecting commission
Providing regular updates, servicing support, online access to investment and portfolio valuation/capital-gains information, and handling investor queries and grievances
Offering a buyback guarantee if the investor is dissatisfied with the scheme's performance

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A (p.133), the trail commission framework recognises that the distributor provides ongoing regular updates and various services to the investor. Per p.219, AMCs and several distributors offer online access to investment information as well as portfolio valuation and capital-gains information to investors. Per p.307-p.309, MFDs are part of the servicing infrastructure and support query handling and grievance redressal for investors. The Trap: Options A and D imply guarantees that no distributor can provide — mutual funds are market-linked products. Option B describes a purely transactional approach that ignores the ongoing service that justifies trail commission. Note: Account statements are issued by the AMC/Registrar; distributors typically support clients in accessing and interpreting them rather than issuing them.
